body: Will note, would like this to be tested by others to make sure I am not breaking other tiling modes or complex situations I might not have thought of. My understanding is that the tile map layer is currently lacking automated tests at the very least, so any testing I've done so far is purely manual. However, was recommended that I attempt to merge this fix in the issue discussion, and if any additional changes are needed (documentation, unit tests, etc) please let me know!

FYI I've started to write some unit tests here with the intention of validating the changes: https://github.com/jynus/godot/commit/9e2fb7eda323076e18191c66714ddfb7f11977f4 (but I haven't finished yet).

Have been testing this with several of the open issues in the [Tiles](https://github.com/orgs/godotengine/projects/46/views/1) todo list to try to get a good exposure to several tilesets. Seems to fix some other existing issues (e.g. #64674 #64769 #73903 ) but have also run into a few potential issues. 

First a tileset like the one in #70218 now seems to perform worse because that tileset has multiple tiles specifying the same transition but with different center bits. So for example it will place a grass to water transition tile next to a water to grass transition tile which is not what is desired by that particular setup. However, it was [mentioned](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/70218#issuecomment-1357819146) in the issue that the intention is that this module does not support multiple transitions in that way and that the tileset should be simplified so this might not be an issue.

Secondly, looking at #76493 which is working with a 2x2 bitmask in `match corners` mode, because this change creates constraints between neighbors it will only look at the cells that touch the cell diagonally, which seems undesired for this mode.

I do find that if I re-add the check for overlapping corners to filter out corner constraints specifically for `match corners` mode that issue also appears fixed, but because of the other changes, tiles could only be added when placed by the rect tool as a 2x2 grid or larger. What this means is that placing a single tile would no longer work unless it's at an appropriate location where a connection could be made (it would instead choose a tile that can be properly connected at that location which tends to be the existing tile), whereas previously you would always be able to place a single tile even if there was no valid connection for it. If this would be okay I could add that change, but otherwise will try to see if I can ensure previous behavior.

Pushed the change I mentioned above so that "Match Corners" mode will still function (but will only function when placing multiple tiles at once. When placing a single tile, it will often find that it does not properly match the corners of it's neighbors and therefore the best fit tile that matches the corner constraints tends to be the existing tile instead of forcing a tile that does not fit the scene but does match the center bit to be drawn.

I see that `match corners` is [supposed to be](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/2d/using_tilesets.html#creating-terrain-sets-autotiling) similar to the `corner set` terrain implemented by [tiled](https://doc.mapeditor.org/en/stable/manual/terrain/#using-terrains) which apparently always forces a 2x2 drawing brush when placing tiles in that mode. Might be something to consider, but that feels probably closer to a feature request and if implemented should be done separately.

I have checked the linked issue, but the presented example there is not supported. Tiles do not link "diagonally only".
When you link two tiles diagonally, there's almost no situation where you do not have to modify the two other tiles to create a visually correct path, so I don't really want to support that use case, unless there's a huge demand for it.
I understand this can be annoying, but sadly the algorithm is rather complex and user relies on it now, so I don't really want to modify it much, especially as it could be compatibility-breaking.

I had this old PR that ended up in limbo but fixed some situations: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/72030
I guess it could be rebased (if anyone wants to do it they are welcome :) )

In the end, I think that, if we rework the terrain system, I'd prefer we implement a new and more robust system. Probably with a dedicated type of TileMapLayers (see https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10572 ). This would allow implementing systems like the ones in LDtk (with special, custom rules), or the dual-grid system.
But in the meantime, I'd rather limit the amount of changes we do to the algorithm to avoid breaking people's projects.

Ah, gotcha, that's understandable! I have been worried about potentially breaking other use cases, and it makes sense to just avoid that entirely, especially because of how difficult it is to verify use cases right now. 

It wasn't clear from the [existing documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/2d/using_tilesets.html#creating-terrain-sets-autotiling) that this was an unsupported case (and judging by the number of issues I saw when trying to test this out, it's apparently a semi-common confusion?), but I'm happy to accept that this is the expected behavior for now until a better system can be implemented.

It's funny that you mentioned the dual-grid system here, because that's actually how I initially stumbled upon this problem in the first place, because instead of wanting to implement it directly, I figured I could autogenerate all 256 tiles from a set of 15 to essentially 'align' the grids into a single layer. Noticed that that effort ended up being a waste because a majority of those tiles were essentially unused with the current autotiling behavior and wanted to understand why. Also the deterministic solution for the 3x3 case here essentially is just making constraints assuming that the center tiles are all consistent terrains anyway like a dual-grid system (and should be equivalent to creating the constraints directly from the proposed terrain layer).

Also looking at #72030 I see that the solution there in `_set_cells_terrain_connect` was essentially my initial solution before I worked on ensuring draw order did not matter. Could potentially give it a shot although it looks like there was some pushback at adding that additional draw mode as well.

Having a decentish understanding of the algorithm now having studied and played with it for the last week or so, I wouldn't be opposed to maybe doing proof of concept work for the proposal either if that's desired.

@groud I've been looking into the code for the constraints system recently. Any chance I could take a shot at cleaning it up?

My goal is just to improve clarity for now, without changing the algorithm or behaviour. Should make considering changes/improvements easier.

> @groud I've been looking into the code for the constraints system recently. Any chance I could take a shot at cleaning it up?

I mean, I guess it depends on the changes? 

But in general we don't really accept code change for the sake of it though, to avoid any regressions. So if it does not bring any performance improvements and is just code style change, I don't think it will be merged.
